title: Stack service settings, one outgoing-header allocation, and owned callback results
comparison: Each fwp service scope versus plain fwp state updates at 1/32/128 calls, O2, collection disabled. Managed requests, requested bytes and final charged storage from constant initialization through main cleanup. Fixed scheduler startup remains included in rows; per-call slopes subtract fixed costs.
limits: Not elapsed time, peak/process memory or C/Rust parity. Excludes raw TLS/capture buffers, allocator metadata and pages. Plain programs omit service fields; their task sizes are not the old service-task baseline. Whole services and remote results remain outside checked ARC support.

binary_observations.observed_change: After the second fwp_apply_owned at 0xbe20, the new function restores registers and returns the result directly in x0 at 0xbe38. The baseline loads record fields at 0xbe40, releases the old record at 0xbecc, and has a new 24-byte allocation path at 0xc048..0xc050 before rebuilding fields. Those operations are absent from the new function. The C worker w10 is inlined into f10 and has no separate binary symbol.

binary_observations.observed_change: The new code calls fwp_apply_owned at 0xcdee, restores its stack and saved registers, and returns the callback result unchanged in rax at 0xcdfe. The baseline releases the old tuple at 0xcec7 and includes a 24-byte allocator slow path at 0xd041..0xd048; these are absent from the new function. Baseline reserves 136 stack bytes plus six saved 8-byte registers; new code reserves 88 plus four saved registers.
